headline: A 2015 law lets certain temporary Interior Department land management workers compete for permanent federal jobs under specific conditions.
what_it_does: Employees of certain Interior Department land management agencies who hold time-limited or temporary competitive-service jobs can apply for permanent positions if they meet set conditions. Those conditions include a competitive original appointment, more than 24 months of time-limited service without a break of two or more years, and acceptable performance. The law also requires the Office of Personnel Management or other examining agency to waive age requirements for these time-limited employees unless age is essential to the job. Former employees who left for reasons other than misconduct or performance can still qualify if they apply within two years of separation.

who_it_affects.group: Temporary and time-limited employees at certain Interior Department land management agencies
who_it_affects.how: They may become eligible to compete for permanent appointments if they meet the service length, original-appointment, and performance conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Former time-limited employees of land management agencies
who_it_affects.how: They can be treated as time-limited employees for this law if they apply within two years of leaving and did not leave due to misconduct or performance.

who_it_affects.group: Older job applicants for competitive-service positions
who_it_affects.how: Age requirements must be waived for covered time-limited employees unless age is essential to the duties of the position.

who_it_affects.group: Office of Personnel Management and examining agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must apply the age waiver and the eligibility rules when examining or appointing covered employees.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted August 7, 2015. The summary does not describe a separate later start date for its provisions.
